standard_prerequisites.name: The two random integers
standard_prerequisites.statement: J_x = prod_{i>=1} e^{h(Y_i)} is the integer-friendly product, and J_x^* is Arratia's random integer defined by the ordered indexing of the transformed point process R^*.
standard_prerequisites.use: The statement compares the two and the proof computes both products over the index sets B_+ and B_-.

standard_prerequisites.name: The good events E_1, E_2, E_3
standard_prerequisites.statement: E_1, E_2, E_3 are the events displayed immediately before the lemma, controlling the spacing sums S_1, S_0, the error R_x and the ordering of the ratios W_i Y_i / h(Y_i).
standard_prerequisites.use: Each event is consumed at a different place: E_1 at lines 850-864, E_2 and E_3 at lines 866-877.

standard_prerequisites.name: von Mangoldt function
standard_prerequisites.statement: Lambda(n) = log p if n is a prime power p^k and 0 otherwise.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the weight h used in the products J_x and in the section's construction, retained in the context.

core_obligations: Assume E_1 occurs, write log J_x as the sum of h(Y_i) over i >= 1 and bound it above by S_1 + R_x + r_0 < log x, using r(Y_1) <= r_0 (source lines 850-855).
Bound log(J_x e^{h(Y_0)}) below by S_0 - R_x - 2 r_0 > log x, and deduce the pair of inequalities J_x < x < J_x e^{h(Y_0)} together with Y_0 > e^{-gamma} (source lines 856-864).

Assume E_2 and E_3 as well, introduce the sets B_+ and B_- of indices with Y_i > e^{-gamma} and rewrite the occurrence of E_2, E_3 as the two ratio inequalities for i in B_+ and i in B_- (source lines 866-876).

Identify the ordered indexing (T_j^*, Q_j^*) of R^* given in the previous section, choose j_0 with T_{j_0}^* = W_0 Y_0 / h(Y_0), and compute the two products over j > j_0 and j >= j_0 as J_x and e^{h(Y_0)} J_x respectively (source lines 877-881).
Combine with J_x < x < J_x e^{h(Y_0)} to conclude j_0 = 0, hence J_x^* = J_x, and finish the probability bound by the union bound over the three events (source lines 844-847 and 881).

proof_roadmap.step: Under E_1, bound log J_x above.
Bound log(J_x e^{h(Y_0)}) below and record J_x < x < J_x e^{h(Y_0)}.
Translate E_2 and E_3 into the two ordering inequalities on B_+ and B_-.
Compare the products indexed by R^* with J_x and force the index j_0 to vanish.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `lem:decomposition J neq J*` at source lines 842-848: if the three events E_1, E_2, E_3 hold then J_x = J_x^*, and consequently the probability that J_x differs from J_x^* is bounded by the sum of the three failure probabilities. The author's proof (source lines 850-882) is a two-stage argument in which the events are used for different purposes: E_1 alone gives the pinching inequalities J_x < x < J_x e^{h(Y_0)} through two separate estimates of log J_x from above and below (lines 852-864), while E_2 and E_3 are converted into the ordering inequalities for the index sets B_+ and B_- (lines 867-876) which are then used to identify the products indexed by the ordered process R^* with the two products built from J_x (lines 877-881). The last step, concluding that the index j_0 must be zero, is what turns the pinching into the equality J_x^* = J_x; none of this structure is visible from the statement.
